# C15 — Paśu / Bounded Subject-Position

## #0

In the Śaiva field, Paśu is the bounded knower/actor whose powers are contracted into a finite horizon. The position has real capacities. It can know, desire, choose, encounter and answer; its boundedness is the condition of these particular acts rather than their simple negation.

Through [tattvic differentiation](../A09-Tattvic-Differential-Field.md), the bounded knower arises through determinate powers and their relations. This efficacy and this horizon of knowledge make a particular encounter possible; desire, time and order give it direction, succession and circumstance. Contraction produces these differentiated capacities, beyond what subtracting one quantity called freedom from an otherwise complete individual could explain.

## #1

Through [Māyā's measure](C14-Maya-Operative-Measure.md), the horizon reveals and withholds. Its contracted capacities mean that an act occurs through this efficacy, this knowledge, this desire, this time and this order. The bounded position receives a field already differentiated enough for something to count as available, absent, possible or excluded.

In the [sixfold tattvic articulation](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md), Puruṣa is the bounded experient within the contracted field; the inner instrument, faculties and material world articulate what can be experienced and acted upon. The local position is located through these relations without being exhausted as their inventory.

## #2

The distinction between universal and local “I am this” matters. Sadāśiva's subjectward orientation and Īśvara's objectward orientation concern the whole appearing field. An egoic appropriation of a particular `x` has a different scope. The same grammatical form cannot erase the difference between self-awareness and a local determination presenting itself as the whole self.

Recognition [[quilt/27-07-26-QUILTING-FOR-FULL-ARGUMENT#3. The Māyic-threshold delineation — the eight determinations' mythic recapitulation (Frank-locked)|precedes egoic appropriation]] in Taylor's primordial I-am relation. The primordial “I am” is not produced by a later individual's claim that a role, body or possession is its exhaustive identity. In the world-parent image, self-recognition precedes the narrated husband/wife division. The [Subject](C01-Subject-Defined-Indefinability.md) is the unobjectifiable pole already presupposed when an identity is known; the [inner instrument](C16-Antahkarana-Inner-Instrument.md) determines and appropriates particular contents. Its appropriation can itself be recognised.

This distinction prevents a reversal of dependence. “I am the holder of this office” can identify a real responsibility without making the office the origin of the “I am.” Losing or revising the office can transform the person's world without proving that subjectivity has been manufactured or annihilated by the change.

## #3

In [Dyczkowski's account of reflective activity](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/indian-philosophy/dyczkowski/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration.md), pp.71–75, individual cognition retains, recalls and recomposes. A goal-bound act pursues a particular result; unrestricted agency makes the formation of goals possible. The bounded knower's movement is a living orientation whose determination can either disclose or conceal its wider condition, rather than a static quantity of missing freedom.

Recognising contraction keeps situated capacity available. Through [recognition](C19-Pratyabhijna-Recognition.md), the local act returns toward the source it continues to express. Its manner of belonging and appropriation changes while its particular life remains to be lived.

## #4

[Prompt thrownness](C44-Prompt-Thrownness.md) gives inherited boundedness a technical form. A local act begins within an already configured horizon: instructions appoint a task, retrieved material makes some things available, retained history carries earlier encounters, permissions delimit possible actions. [Objective Internality](C41-Objective-Internality.md) names the operative world constituted through those relations.

A particular contraction becomes investigable through its consequences. An unavailable tool limits efficacy; an omitted source limits what can be known; a time horizon selects which events can count; an evaluation rule orders what is preferred. Altering one does not automatically alter the others. Giving an agent a broader description of its commission, for example, does not grant permission to execute a new action. The return must reach the condition that actually bounds the act.

Responsibility follows the same articulation. An agent can answer for an act within its powers; a designer or operator remains answerable for a withheld capability, imposed criterion or inaccessible source that governs the act. Naming the agent a bounded participant makes these relations more exact, rather than transferring every condition to a fictitiously self-originating actor. The comparison concerns this enacted distribution of capacity and responsibility; paśu retains its fuller Śaiva genealogy.

## #5→0

Through [Māyā's eye, veil, frame and horizon](../../../symbolon/mytheme/worlds/frank-taylor/maya-eye-veil-frame-horizon/WHOLE.md#maya-measure-dream), limited agency, knowledge, desire, time and order make a bounded life capable of acting here. The eye sees from a particular angle; the dream becomes an objective world within its experience. Recognition recovers the condition whose withdrawal let that world appear self-standing. The differentiated position remains, with its source relation available.

The primordial recognition and subsequent ego-identity have distinct offices in Taylor's correction. In the [world-parent separation](../../../symbolon/mytheme/archetypal-ground/neumann-images/WHOLE.md#neumann-world-parent-separation), self-recognition precedes the husband/wife division; bounded knowing arises within that field rather than making ego identity its origin. Through the [uroboros's differentiated body](../../../symbolon/mytheme/archetypal-ground/uroboros-trickster/WHOLE.md#uroboros-source-variants), head, tail, mouth and winding keep the opening through which the creature receives, transforms and returns. The formed body's efficacy remains related to the condition it cannot fill.

Through [[symbolon/episteme/etymologies/trust-place-logos-nomos-natio-credere/WHOLE-FIELD|Trust / Place / Logos / Nomos / Natio / Credere]], the place of an act bears its conditions and commitments. A bounded participant answers from somewhere, under particular permissions and with particular means. Their judgment can be corrected under fitting conditions, or a failed condition can be returned to the office capable of changing it. Reasons for retaining a fitting condition remain available with that judgment. The next act inherits this answerability through actual capacity. The relation joins situated place and bounded knowing while keeping the Greek and Sanskrit lexical histories distinct.

The horizon remains real while its source relation becomes available. Recognition leaves a particular knower able to act without claiming to be the origin of every condition of action. Its finite powers can now be exercised, relinquished or revised in awareness of what they owe to the wider field. Situated responsibility carries that changed relation into the next encounter.
